theory.overview: Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a weighted undirected graph is a subset of edges that connects all vertices with minimum total weight and no cycles. MST has V-1 edges for V vertices. Two classic algorithms: Prim's (greedy, grows tree from vertex) and Kruskal's (greedy, adds edges in weight order, uses Union-Find). MSTs are used in network design, clustering, and approximation algorithms. This chapter covers MST algorithms, their properties, and applications.

sections.title: MST Properties
sections.content: Cut property: For any cut (partition of vertices), minimum weight edge crossing cut is in some MST. Cycle property: For any cycle, maximum weight edge in cycle is not in any MST. MST is unique if all edge weights are distinct. Multiple MSTs possible if some weights equal. MST minimizes total weight while ensuring connectivity.
properties: Cut property: min edge crossing cut is in MST
Cycle property: max edge in cycle not in MST

sections.title: Prim's Algorithm
sections.content: Grows MST from starting vertex. Maintain set of vertices in MST. Repeatedly add minimum weight edge connecting MST to non-MST vertex. Uses min-heap for efficiency. Time: $O(E \log V)$ with heap, $O(V^2)$ without. Space: $O(V+E)$. Similar to Dijkstra but tracks edge weight instead of path weight.
sections.algorithm: Initialize MST with any vertex. Min-heap of edges crossing cut. Extract min, add vertex to MST, add new crossing edges to heap. Repeat until V-1 edges.

sections.title: Kruskal's Algorithm
sections.content: Sorts all edges by weight. Adds edges in increasing order, skipping edges that would create cycle (detected by Union-Find). Time: $O(E \log E)$ for sorting, $O(E \alpha(V))$ for Union-Find. Space: $O(V+E)$. Easier to implement with Union-Find. Good for sparse graphs.
sections.algorithm: Sort edges by weight. For each edge in order: if endpoints in different components, add to MST, union components. Stop when V-1 edges added.

sections.title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
sections.content: Data structure for tracking connected components. Operations: find(x) returns component representative, union(x,y) merges components. Path compression and union by rank ensure near-constant amortized time. Essential for Kruskal's cycle detection.

sections.title: MST Applications
sections.content: Network design: minimum cost to connect all locations (cables, roads). Clustering: single-linkage clustering uses MST. Approximation algorithms: MST-based 2-approximation for TSP. Bottleneck MST: minimize maximum edge weight. Used in image segmentation, facility location.

keyConcepts.name: Cut Property
keyConcepts.description: For any partition of vertices, the minimum weight edge crossing the partition belongs to some MST. Basis for Prim's algorithm.

keyConcepts.name: Cycle Detection
keyConcepts.description: In Kruskal's, edge creates cycle if both endpoints already in same component. Union-Find efficiently tracks components.

keyConcepts.name: Path Compression
keyConcepts.description: In Union-Find, flatten tree structure during find. Makes future finds faster. Near-constant amortized time.

keyConcepts.name: Union by Rank
keyConcepts.description: In Union-Find, attach smaller tree under larger tree's root. Keeps trees shallow, improves performance.

steps.title: Prim's - Initialize
steps.description: Start with any vertex. Add all edges from it to min-heap.
steps.code: mst = {start}; heap = [(w, start, v) for v, w in neighbors[start]];

steps.title: Extract Min Edge
steps.description: Extract minimum weight edge from heap. If both endpoints in MST, skip.
steps.code: w, u, v = heappop(heap); if v in mst: continue;

steps.title: Add to MST
steps.description: Add edge and new vertex to MST. Add all edges from new vertex to heap.
steps.code: mst.add(v); total_weight += w; for new_v, new_w in neighbors[v]: heappush(heap, (new_w, v, new_v));

steps.title: Repeat
steps.description: Continue until MST has V-1 edges.

steps.title: Kruskal's - Sort Edges
steps.description: Sort all edges by weight. Initialize Union-Find with each vertex as separate component.

steps.title: Process Edges
steps.description: For each edge in order: if endpoints in different components, add to MST, union components.
steps.code: for u, v, w in edges: if uf.find(u) != uf.find(v): mst.append((u,v,w)); uf.union(u,v); if len(mst) == V-1: break;

practiceProblems.title: Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to connect all cities (MST).
practiceProblems.solution: Kruskal's with Union-Find. Sort edges, add if connects different components.

practiceProblems.title: Optimize Water Distribution
practiceProblems.description: Minimize cost to provide water (pipes + wells).
practiceProblems.solution: Add virtual well node with edge to each house (well cost). Run MST on this graph.

practiceProblems.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to connect all points (complete graph, edge = Manhattan distance).
practiceProblems.solution: Prim's on complete graph. Or optimize by sorting edges (still O(n² log n)).

practiceProblems.title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges
practiceProblems.description: Find edges that must be in all MSTs (critical) and edges in some MSTs (pseudo-critical).
practiceProblems.solution: For each edge, check if MST without it has same weight (pseudo-critical) or higher weight (critical).
practiceProblems.hints: Check each edge, compare MST weights

practiceProblems.title: The Maze II
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest distance from start to exit (can break walls at cost).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra. Edge to adjacent cell = 1, edge to break wall = cost.

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection
practiceProblems.description: Find edge that can be removed to make tree (n nodes, n edges, one cycle).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find. Add edges one by one. If edge connects already connected components, it's redundant.

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection II
practiceProblems.description: Find edge to remove in graph with two possible cycles.
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find with parent tracking. Handle cases: edge to same node, multiple parents.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum operations to connect all computers (can add cable between any two).
practiceProblems.solution: Count connected components. Need components - 1 cables. If cables < n-1, return -1.

practiceProblems.title: Maximize Network Quality
practiceProblems.description: Maximize minimum quality edge in MST (bottleneck MST).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on threshold or use Prim's with max-heap for min edge.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Spanning Tree (Prim's)
practiceProblems.description: Implement Prim's algorithm to find MST weight.
practiceProblems.solution: Start from any vertex. Min-heap of crossing edges. Extract min, add vertex, repeat.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Spanning Tree (Kruskal's)
practiceProblems.description: Implement Kruskal's algorithm to find MST weight.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort edges by weight. Union-Find to detect cycles. Add edges until V-1.

practiceProblems.title: Union-Find Implementation
practiceProblems.description: Implement Union-Find with path compression and union by rank.
practiceProblems.solution: Array for parent and rank. Find with path compression. Union by rank.

practiceProblems.title: Accounts Merge
practiceProblems.description: Merge accounts with same email (each account has list of emails).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on emails. Accounts with same email connected. Group by root.

practiceProblems.title: Sentence Similarity II
practiceProblems.description: Check if sentences are similar given similarity pairs (transitive).
practiceProblems.solution: Build graph from pairs. Union-Find on words. Check if each word pair connected.

practiceProblems.title: Graph Valid Tree
practiceProblems.description: Check if graph is valid tree (n nodes, n-1 edges, connected, no cycles).
practiceProblems.solution: Check n-1 edges. Union-Find: if edge connects already connected components, cycle. Check if one component at end.
practiceProblems.hints: Union-Find, check n-1 edges and one component

practiceProblems.title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
practiceProblems.description: Check if equality equations are satisfiable (a==b, b==c, a!=c → false).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find for equalities. For inequalities, check if variables in same component.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
practiceProblems.description: Find longest consecutive elements sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash set. For each number, if num-1 not in set, it's sequence start. Count consecutive.
practiceProblems.hints: Hash set, start from sequence starts

practiceProblems.title: Making A Large Island
practiceProblems.description: Change one 0 to 1 to maximize island size in binary matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS to label islands with sizes. For each 0, check adjacent islands, sum sizes + 1.
practiceProblems.hints: Label islands with DFS, check each 0

practiceProblems.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
practiceProblems.description: Find max stones that can be removed (stone removed if shares row/col with another).
practiceProblems.solution: Union-Find on rows and columns. Each connected component can have one stone left.

practiceProblems.title: Swim in Rising Water
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum time to swim from top-left to bottom-right (water rises over time).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra variant or binary search on time with BFS/DFS.

practiceProblems.title: Path With Minimum Effort
practiceProblems.description: Find path minimizing maximum height difference.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra variant: min-heap by max effort.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to make at least one valid path from 1 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra on modified graph with edge costs for direction changes.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Score of Path Between Two Cities
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum score path (score = min edge weight on path).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra variant: max-heap by min edge weight on path.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Performance of a Team
practiceProblems.description: Select k engineers to maximize performance (sum(speed) × min(efficiency)).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by efficiency descending. Maintain min-heap of k speeds. Calculate performance at each step.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort by efficiency, min-heap of speeds

practiceProblems.title: Find Critical Pseudo-Critical Edges
practiceProblems.description: Find critical and pseudo-critical edges in MST.
practiceProblems.solution: For each edge, compute MST without it and with it forced. Compare weights.
practiceProblems.hints: Compare MST with and without each edge

Prim's Algorithm
snippets.code:
import heapq

def prim(graph, start):
    V = len(graph)
    visited = [False] * V
    heap = [(0, start, -1)]  # (weight, vertex, parent)
    mst_weight = 0
    edges_used = 0
    
    while heap and edges_used < V - 1:
        w, u, parent = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if visited[u]:
            continue
        visited[u] = True
        mst_weight += w
        edges_used += 1
        
        for v, weight in graph[u]:
            if not visited[v]:
                heapq.heappush(heap, (weight, v, u))
    
    return mst_weight
